staff.skill_evidence_note: staff-1/staff-2 are now bound to two real named strategy-guide candidates (manda_machiko / sugawara_fumio out of the 35-person roster in staff_candidates below) rather than an arbitrary flat 20/15/15 placeholder repeated on both slots -- their service_skill/security_skill/cleaning_skill/register_skill/replenishment_skill/salary_yen_per_day_24h/*_skill_growth_ceiling values are CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, ported verbatim from that candidate's guide card (see staff_candidates_evidence_note). register_skill is consumed by CheckoutTiming (task #33) for checkout duration; replenishment_skill is consumed the same way by RestockTiming (task #40) for restock duration. service_skill/security_skill/cleaning_skill are consumed too, since task #27: VerticalSliceSimulation._evaluate_store_rating() collects every staff member's values and feeds them to store_value.gd's compute_service_value/compute_security_value/compute_cleaning_value each month, which roll into the monthly star rating (store_rating.gd). This note previously (incorrectly) claimed those three fields were unconsumed; corrected in task #43 after an audit found the claim had gone stale without anyone updating it. salary_yen_per_day_24h is consumed as of task #47: VerticalSliceSimulation._apply_daily_staff_wages() charges every active staff member once per simulated day. As of task #50, each staff member's salary_yen_per_day_24h is treated as a 24-hour-basis figure and scaled down to demand.opening_minutes_per_day (docs/research/quick-reference-guide-part1-2026-09-19.md section 1.2, CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, stated twice: 人件費...時給×営業時間) rather than charging the flat 24h figure regardless of configured hours; this client still has no shift/hours-worked tracking for *individual* staff, but the guide's own formula scales by the store's configured business hours, not by how many of those hours each staff member personally worked, so no such tracking needs to be invented to apply it. The floor-rounding of the scaling is this project's own REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT choice. As of task #48, the guide's skill-growth model (work-event counting) is also wired: StaffGrowth.apply_checkout_growth()/apply_replenish_growth() (game/scripts/domain/staff_growth.gd) grow register_skill+service_skill on every completed checkout task and replenishment_skill+cleaning_skill+security_skill on every completed restock task, each clamped to that skill's own *_skill_growth_ceiling. Of those five (task, skill) pairs, only replenish->replenishment_skill's +1 magnitude is CONFIRMED_COMMUNITY (reference_sim/conveni_sim/staff_growth_resolution.py's EVIDENCE_BACKED_UNIT_GROWTH); the other four reuse the same +1 as a REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT guess, matching reference_sim/conveni_sim/remake_staff_growth.py's own equivalent default. Not ported: the manager-education growth bonus (no manager designation exists among staff.members here) and clean-task growth (no standalone cleaning task/mechanic exists in this client). Skill growth is also not part of the save/load format yet (see vertical_slice_simulation.gd's save_state() comment) -- a save/load round trip currently reverts accumulated growth.

simulation.checkout_anger_evidence_note: As of task #49, CheckoutAnger (game/scripts/domain/checkout_anger.gd) is wired into VerticalSliceSimulation's checkout phase handling: once per checkout, if the active service runs past CheckoutAnger.trigger_ticks(checkout_ticks), the confirmed -2 penalty is applied and a checkout_anger_triggered event is recorded. As of task #51, the penalty applies to EVERY active staff member's register/replenishment/security/cleaning/service skills (clamped at 0), not only the one who served the customer -- a direct re-read of the strategy guide's own book pages 34-35 (店員全員の能力が下がってしまう, every staff member's ability drops) confirmed this CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, superseding task #49's original single-staff-member scoping. The -2 penalty magnitude itself is CONFIRMED_COMMUNITY (first-title dedicated research; PROJECT_MEMORY.md section 6: low register_skill can make checkout extremely slow and cause customer anger), but reference_sim/conveni_sim/checkout_anger_timing.py deliberately leaves the trigger threshold to a caller-supplied policy ('the coordinator never invents an anger threshold') and checkout_anger_penalty.py leaves the floor unconfirmed too. This project's REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT choices: the floor reuses 0, the same non-negative floor already enforced on every skill field elsewhere in this codebase; the trigger threshold is anchored to CheckoutTiming's own already-confirmed reference duration (task #33) rather than an unrelated new number -- anger fires once actual service ticks exceed TRIGGER_MULTIPLIER (2.0) times the reference (median-register_skill) duration, so a staff member at or above the reference register_skill (both staff-1/staff-2 are) never triggers it; only a below-reference hire risks angering a customer, matching the guide's own causal story.
simulation.eject_customer_evidence_note: Task #52: try_eject_customer() (VerticalSliceSimulation) lets the player select a customer in the waiting_checkout/checkout phase and remove them from the store before the checkout-anger penalty can trigger, forfeiting their purchase entirely. The mechanic itself is CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, directly re-read from the strategy guide (book p.35): '怒りやすいお客さんは、おじさんやおじいさんに多い。もしレジ前の混雑にこの人が混じっていたら、カーソルをこの人に合わせて決定ボタン。怒り出すまえに"つまみだす"を選んで、お店の外に出してしまうといいぞ。' This project's own REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT choice: an ejected customer's already-picked-up basket units are not returned to shelf stock (no source states this either way, and this client has no other 'undo a pick-up' mechanic to reuse instead of inventing one), so ejecting a customer with a full basket is a real shrinkage cost, not a free do-over.
simulation.price_policy_evidence_note: Task #53: try_set_price_policy(price_change_pct) lets the player set a global price change percentage, consumed both when a customer picks up a product (VerticalSliceSimulation._apply_price_policy() scales the product_catalog's own sale_price_yen) and by the monthly store-rating evaluation (store_rating.gd's price_change_pct input, hardcoded to 0 since task #27). The mechanic itself is CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL, directly re-read from the strategy guide (クイックリファレンス book pages 5-6): a global profit-margin percentage defaulting to 40% ('これが定価と考えられる'), and a screenshot showing a global 'all items X% off list price' slider plus a per-item override. This project only ports the global slider -- the per-item override is a REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT scope choice, not implemented. simulation.staff_hiring_evidence_note: Task #56: VerticalSliceSimulation.try_hire_candidate(staff_id, candidate_id) lets the player replace whoever currently occupies an existing staff.members roster slot with a different candidate drawn from the same 35-person staff_candidates pool (task #32, CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL). This project's own REMAKE_BALANCED_DEFAULT scope choices: this client's staff.members roster stays a fixed 2 slots and 'hiring' means swapping the occupant of an existing slot, not adding a 3rd slot -- neither the 店長 (manager) role/slot nor the スーパー社員 (super employee, an aging-to-elder-triggered stat-maxing mechanic per PROJECT_MEMORY.md section 21.3) is implemented; both are explicitly out of scope (see docs/decisions/0125-*.md).
